title: Marcelo Goffman : A quantum circuit harnessing both the bosonic and the fermionic side of the Josephson effect
description: Abstract Superconducting artificial atoms rely on Josephson junctions, whose quantum variable is the phase difference φ, a collective electromagnetic degree of freedom of the condensate. Yet, every Josephson weak link also hosts a fermionic degree of freedom: the occupation of Andreev bound states by quasiparticles.This second quantum variable can encode qubits when the weak link is highly transparent and a magnetic flux threading a small-inductance loop imposes a classical phase φ across it. Up to now, every explored circuit exploits the quantumness of just one of these degrees of freedom, while the other stays frozen. What happens when a transparent weak link is embedded in a large-inductance circuit, so that both degrees of freedom are dynamical? Bosonic and fermionic excitations hybridize, opening regimes where the circuit low-energy states are protected against relaxation and, at sweet spots, against dephasing. I will discuss this circuit, which we call FerBo, and present a first implementation based on an InAs/Al nanowire weak link and a Josephson-junction-array superinductance. Marcelo Goffman, Quantronics Group, Service de Physique de l’Etat Condensé, CEA-CNRS, CEA-Saclay, 91191 Gif-sur-Yvette Cedex, France

title: Diego Garcia Ovalle : Spin and orbital angular momentum in periodic solids: From nonmagnetic to magnetic materials
description: Speaker: Diego Garcia Ovalle, Postdoctoral Fellow, Sherbrooke University Location : LPS Theo Coffee Room + Zoom Abstract: Over the past few years, the study of the electron’s degrees of freedom have received a major interest in condensed matter, both theoretically and experimentally. In particular, investigating the spin and the orbital angular momentum is a source of a fascinating landscape of new physics in periodic systems, where materials that are effectively nonmagnetic and even composed with light elements can be used for the new generation of more efficient electronic devices. In this talk, I will explain from the theory point of view how these two fundamental properties of the electron have a dramatic impact on the nonequilibrium responses of quantum materials. Firstly, in the nonmagnetic case, I will describe how the angular momentum of the electron can be connected to the nonlinear Hall effect in noncentrosymmetric materials. When moving forward to analyze spin and orbital transport exclusively, I will focus on distinguishing the role of spin-orbit coupling and the Rashba effect on the spin and orbital-to-charge conversion in materials without inversion symmetry, which are key figures of merit for the optimization of the basic structures in data storage. Secondly, we will switch the gear to ferromagnetic materials to discuss two distinct effects in low symmetry crystals that emerge from the trigonal warping of the Fermi surface: A special class of spin-orbit torque and the so-called crystalline in-plane Hall effect. Last but not least, I will present an important prospect of my work that aims to exploit the spin and the orbital angular momentum in antiferromagnets and altermagnets from surface engineering. Here, I will illustrate the instance of the nonequilibrium spin polarization reported very recently, and its potential extension to superconductivity. Exploring nonequilibrium responses arising on the spin or the angular momentum serve not only as a probe of the electronic structure of quantum materials, but also as tools that might shed light on how to control them externally for novel applications in spin-orbitronics.

description: Abstract:The Onsager algebra plays an important role in exactly solvable models. The talk is based on a series of work in arXiv: 2606.25660, 2103.14569, 2012.10224 and work in progress.

title: Étude de l’évolution de la cristallographie et de la chimie des ciments durables pendant leur carbonatation accélérée
description: Étude de l’évolution de la cristallographie et de la chimie des ciments durables pendant leur carbonatation accélérée Le 2 novembre 2026 Types d’événements Thèses ou HDR Intervenant Valentin Hérault NIMBE/LIONS Localisation Amphi Claude Bloch, Bât 774, CEA Saclay, Site de L’Orme des merisiers Période Le 2 novembre 2026 Heures de 14h00 à 17h00 Facebook LinkedIn La production de ciment est responsable de 8 à 10 % des émissions mondiales anthropiques de CO 2 . Comme solution pour réduire les émissions de CO 2 et valoriser le CO 2 , l’utilisation de la réaction entre le CO 2 et les matériaux ci mentaires pour le durcissement est une approche prometteuse. Cependant, la carbonatation du ci ment implique de nombreux phénomènes physico chimiques couplés et dépend de la formulation du ciment, de la composition du mélange et des conditions de cure. Cela rend l’élaboration et la validation de modèles prédictifs difficiles, car ceux-ci nécessitent des données expérimentales étendues pour optimiser le processus de carbonatation. La plupart des méthodes de suivi de la carbonatation nécessitant un échantillonnage destructif, la résolution temporelle et la compréhension de la cinétique de carbonatation sont limitées, et la plupart des jeux de données expérimentaux sont fragmentés sur plusieurs échantillons. Ce travail répond à cette lacune en développant, validant et appliquant des techniques de caractérisation operando non destructives, capables de suivre un même échantillon tout au long de la carbonatation accélérée. La première partie de ce travail porte sur la conception et la validation d’un microréacteur imprimé en 3D pour le contrôle de flux de gaz, permettant le suivi operando d’échantillons de ciment au cours de carbonatation sous concentration en CO 2 et humidité relative contrôlées. La réduction de l’échelle de l’échantillon de deux ordres de grandeur par rapport aux échantillons conventionnels a permis de réduire les temps de carbonatation de plusieurs semaines à quelques heures et a rendu possible la réalisation de mesures de diffraction des rayons X (DRX) en transmission, non destructives, pour suivre les échantillons en cours de carbonatation. Le dispositif a été validé et appliqué à la carbonatation d’échantillons millimétriques de chaux et de ciment Portland ordinaire sous une large gamme de concentrations en CO 2 et d’humidités relatives. La cinétique de carbonatation a été caractérisée en comparant la quantification Rietveld des données de DRX avec un modèle basé sur la diffusion, révélant une forte influence des conditions environnementales sur la vitesse de carbonatation. La deuxième partie de ce travail porte sur une autre lacune des techniques conventionnelles de suivi de la carbonatation, à savoir la résolution spatiale limitée. Des mesures operando de profils linéaires par spectroscopie Raman et DRX de laboratoire, ainsi que des cartographies operando 2D par DRX en synchrotron, ont été réalisées pour suivre l’évolution de la composition

title: Manuel BIBES : Oxide spintronics
description: Transition metal oxides, particularly those with a perovskite structure, exhibit an extraordinary diversity of electronic and magnetic properties, often strongly tunable by external stimuli. This makes them a particularly rich playground for spintronics, which aims to exploit the electron spin to store, process and transmit information. In this seminar, I will give a broad overview of how oxides have contributed to the development of spintronics and continue to open new directions. I will first discuss manganites, whose half-metallic ferromagnetism provides highly spin-polarized currents, and multiferroic materials, which enable the control of magnetism by electric fields. I will then turn to oxide interfaces hosting two-dimensional electron gases, where strong spin-orbit coupling allows the efficient interconversion between charge and spin currents through the Edelstein effects. Finally, I will show how combining these functionalities with ferroelectricity provides a route towards nonvolatile electrical control of spin-charge interconversion, opening perspectives for ultralow-power memory and logic devices. Biographie : Manuel Bibes is a CNRS Research Director at the Laboratoire Albert Fert Fert (CNRS, Thales, Université Paris-Saclay) in Palaiseau, France. After engineering studies at INSA Toulouse (1998) and a double PhD degree in France and Spain with a thesis on manganite interfaces (ICMAB Barcelona, 2001) he became a CNRS Researcher in 2003. Bibes has pioneered research lines on multiferroics, ferroelectric tunnel junctions and explored novel routes for the electrical control of magnetism, spin-charge interconversion and spin transport in oxide architectures. Bibes is the laureate of three ERC grants and a Highly Cited Researcher. He has received several awards including the Descartes-Huygens Prize in 2017, the EuroPhysics Prize in 2022 and the CNRS Silver Medal in 2025. In October 2024, he co-founded the start-up NELLOW that develops and aims to commercialize ultralow power chips for AI and logic based on quantum oxide materials.

title: Chisa Hotta : Typicality of Quantum States
description: Speaker : Chisa Hotta, Professor, University of Tokyo Abstract: Quantum many-body systems in thermal equilibrium are conventionally described by the Gibbs state, which involves an exponentially large number of basis states for a system of size (N). Its direct construction and manipulation therefore become practically infeasible for sufficiently large systems. However, studies since the early 2000s have established that one can often bypass the Gibbs ensemble and instead use a single pure state randomly chosen from a microcanonical energy shell. Such a state can reproduce the expectation values of local observables with high accuracy, equivalent to those obtained from the Gibbs ensemble. This remarkable property is known as canonical typicality or, more broadly, thermal typicality. We have been developing a method to construct such thermal typical states using matrix product states (MPS), which we call thermal pure quantum MPS (TPQ-MPS). The basic idea is to start from a random state representing the infinite-temperature limit and cool it down to a target temperature through imaginary-time evolution. In principle, a sufficiently entangled pure state can encode the full thermal entropy, with its entanglement entropy following a volume law. In practice, however, the entanglement that can be stored in an MPS is limited by the available computational resources. We compensate for this limitation by introducing random sampling and averaging, which effectively incorporates the missing entropy and leads to states that are neither fully pure nor fully mixed. This provides a framework to classify thermal-state representations according to their degree of purity, ranging from the Gibbs ensemble to a fully developed thermal pure quantum (TPQ) state. We will discuss how this classification can be quantified, how it depends on the available computational resources, and how TPQ-MPS can be applied to thermal states of two-dimensional quantum systems, including the Kitaev model. The concept of typicality also extends to nonequilibrium dynamics. By evolving a single TPQ state in real time, one can reproduce thermal ensemble dynamics without explicitly handling the exponentially large Gibbs state. This dynamical typicality offers a powerful route to long-time quantum dynamics, beyond the time scales accessible to many conventional numerical approaches. If time permits, we will also discuss ongoing developments toward variational approaches for constructing thermal states. Related papers: A Iwaki, A Shimizu, C Hotta, Phys. Rev. title: Towards Efficient and Autonomous Neutron Scattering Experiments
description: Towards Efficient and Autonomous Neutron Scattering Experiments Le 3 novembre 2026 Types d’événements Séminaire LLB Intervenant Elliott Perryman ILL (Institut Laue Langevin) Localisation LLB – Bât 563 p15 (Grande Salle) Période Le 3 novembre 2026 Heures de 11h00 à 12h00 Facebook LinkedIn Magnetic neutron scattering experiments take days of scarce beam-time, even with high neutron fluxes. Because neutron beamtime is so valuable, extracting the most physics information from the available neutrons is critical. One way to extract more information without hardware improvements is autonomous experimental design. These are algorithmic approaches that control a neutron scattering experiment to reduce the time needed to characterize S(q, ω). Programmatically steering neutron experiments requires a quantitative understanding of the efficiency of an experiment and on-line analysis of data, both of which can be interesting even for an expert user. I will present a method for autonomous experiments that aims to free users from the minutia of tracking a signal’s evolution, which provides time for live analysis of their experiment. This method exploits the smoothness of the dynamic structure factor S(Q, ω) to build a surrogate S(Q, ω) model that is used to sequentially choose (Q,ω) points. The resulting method has been simulated to effectively track a dispersion curve, even in low signal with poor signal to noise. Such efforts are required to reach our goal of fully autonomous and efficient neutron experiments. title: Toward the CompactHedron: Bounds on Neutron Stars from Microscopic Principles
description: Much is still unknown about neutron stars, including their equation of state, which describes the matter in their interior. Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors can help shed light on this question by measuring the so-called Love numbers, which encode the tidal response of a compact object to an external perturbation. In this talk, I will investigate the implications of causality and positivity for the tidal Love numbers of gravitating objects. I will work within the framework of point-particle effective field theory, where the Love numbers correspond to the Wilson coefficients of operators constructed from the curvature tensor. I will show that requiring the tidal response to be retarded and to decay at high frequencies, together with the assumption of passivity, leads to nontrivial bounds on the Love numbers. I will then outline the computation of dynamical Love numbers through fourth order in the frequency expansion, using dimensional regularization, for a representative set of neutron-star equations of state, and show that, in the low-compactness regime, the bounds translate into constraints on the fundamental oscillation mode of the star. While the focus is primarily on conservative systems, I will also discuss how the bounds are modified in the presence of dissipation. These results lay the groundwork for a systematic framework to derive bounds on compact objects from fundamental principles.

title: Wladimir A Benalcazar : Spatial Localizers: Where Electrons and Excitons Live in Quantum Matter
description: Speaker: Wladimir A Benalcazar, Assistant Professor of Physics, Emory University Electron localization underlies chemical bonding, polarization, and band topology, yet beyond one dimension no general framework exists to determine where electrons sit in an insulator. I will introduce the spatial localizer, an operator whose spectrum locates electrons in two- and three-dimensional insulators, including those with boundaries, defects, and disorder. It yields a position-space bulk-defect correspondence for charge and maximally localized states that reduce to Wannier functions in atomic insulators and to Landau-level-like coherent states in Chern insulators. I will then extend this idea to excitons, where simultaneous localization of electron and hole is obstructed by the quantum geometric dipole. An exciton spatial localizer overcomes this, producing constituent-resolved exciton Wannier functions without gauge fixing or optimization.

title: Ouverture des inscriptions pour les French Photonics Days 2026
description: Ouverture des inscriptions pour les French Photonics Days 2026 Fil d'Ariane Accueil Agenda Ouverture des inscriptions pour les French Photonics Days 2026 × Envoyer cette page à un ami Ouverture des inscriptions pour les French Photonics Days 2026 Les inscriptions sont désormais ouvertes pour la 8ᵉ édition des French Photonics Days , qui se tiendra les 9 et 10 novembre 2026 à la Maison MINATEC , à Grenoble. Organisé par Photonics France , SupOptique Alumni et Minalogic , avec le soutien du CEA-Leti , d' Optica , de l' IESF – Ingénieurs et Scientifiques de France et de la Société Française d'Optique (SFO) , cet événement s'est imposé comme un rendez-vous incontournable pour la communauté photonique. La photonique au cœur des technologies de demain Placée sous le thème « Photonique et innovation : la lumière au cœur des technologies de demain » , cette nouvelle édition proposera un panorama des avancées les plus récentes dans le domaine de la photonique et de leurs nombreuses applications. Conçu pour un public technique, sans nécessiter une expertise approfondie du domaine, le programme permettra aux participantes et participants de : découvrir les dernières innovations et les nouveaux développements des technologies photoniques ; mieux comprendre leurs applications dans de nombreux secteurs industriels et scientifiques ; échanger autour des travaux de recherche présentés par des doctorantes et doctorants ; visiter exceptionnellement des entreprises et des plateformes technologiques grenobloises, au cœur de l'un des principaux écosystèmes français de l'innovation. Un temps fort pour la communauté photonique Les French Photonics Days constituent chaque année un espace privilégié de rencontres entre les acteurs académiques, industriels et institutionnels de la filière. Conférences, présentations de travaux de recherche et visites techniques offriront aux participants une vision concrète des innovations qui façonneront les technologies de demain. Les inscriptions sont d'ores et déjà ouvertes : lien vers la billetterie . Le programme détaillé est également disponible . Enfin, les entreprises et organisations souhaitant associer leur image à cet événement peuvent encore rejoindre les partenaires des French Photonics Days 2026 grâce aux différentes offres de sponsoring proposées .

title: Séminaire Qilin Zhou
description: Lanthanide-Doped Luminescent Nanorods as Optical Probes for Measuring Flow-Induced Shear and Mechanical Strain Dr. Qilin Zou, Laboratory for Vascular Translational Science (LVTS), INSERM, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord (Paris 13), Université Paris Cité Abstract Mechanical forces and deformations play a fundamental role in biological systems, soft materials, and engineering applications. However, their local measurement remains challenging, particularly in complex fluids and deformable materials. In this seminar, I will present our recent work on developing lanthanide-doped luminescent nanorods as versatile optical probes for quantitative mechanical sensing. By regulating the anisotropic morphology and tailoring the polarized luminescence of Eu 3+ -doped LaPO 4 nanorods, we establish an optical sensing approach that translates nanorod collective orientation into a measurable signal, enabling the reliable and accurate measurement of local mechanical environments. I will first introduce our shearmetry strategy, in which flow-induced alignment of luminescent nanorods provides an optical readout of local shear stress. Through the development of size-controlled LaPO 4 :Eu 3+ nanorods, we demonstrate how nanoparticle morphology, particularly nanorod aspect ratio (length/width), governs their orientational dynamics and sensing performance. Combined with the tunable rheological properties of nanorod-based fluids, this approach enables quantitative mapping of shear-stress distributions in microfluidic channels, including complex dynamic flows and non-Newtonian fluids that mimic physiological biofluids. Furthermore, I will explore the extension of polarized luminescence sensing from fluid mechanics to solid-state deformation. By incorporating LaPO 4 :Eu 3+ nanorods into flexible polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrices, we demonstrate reversible optical strain sensing based on deformation-induced nanorod alignment. The resulting changes in polarized Eu 3+ emission provide a quantitative measure of applied strain, while controlling nanorod concentration and aspect ratio offers a means of tailoring sensor sensitivity and operating range. In summary, these studies establish lanthanide-based polarization luminescence as a versatile optical platform for probing mechanical forces across fluid and solid environments. By combining nanomaterial engineering, lanthanide photophysics, and mechanical sensing, this strategy opens new opportunities for spatially resolved mechanical determination, with potential applications in biofluidics, soft robotics, and wearable sensing technologies.

title: [EXPO] Voyage dans l’invisible – Manipulez la matière !
description: Et si vous pouviez voyager au cœur de la matière, explorer l’infiniment petit et manipuler l’invisible du bout des doigts ? Que se cache-t-il derrière les objets qui nous entourent ? Comment les scientifiques parviennent-ils à observer, comprendre et transformer la matière à l’échelle des atomes ? Du grain de sable aux nanomatériaux, des propriétés étonnantes du magnétisme aux mystères des matériaux quantiques, Voyage dans l’invisible – Manipulez la matière ! vous invite à franchir les frontières du visible pour découvrir un monde fascinant, souvent insoupçonné, qui façonne notre quotidien et les technologies de demain. Ici, la science se regarde, se touche et s’expérimente ! Plongez dans l’univers de la physique à travers un parcours immersif et ludique, imaginé par les scientifiques du Laboratoire de Physique des Solides. Observez des objets surprenants, découvrez des expériences étonnantes et laissez-vous guider par votre curiosité. Petits et grands, amateurs de sciences ou simples explorateurs, chacun pourra porter un regard nouveau sur la matière qui nous entoure. Cette exposition est aussi une invitation à découvrir la science autrement : les décors ont été peints à la main, tandis que les objets scientifiques ont été conçus et fabriqués par les ingénieurs du laboratoire ou sont de véritables équipements utilisés dans la recherche. Une occasion unique de découvrir, au plus près, les instruments, les idées et les savoir-faire qui permettent aux scientifiques d’explorer l’invisible. Informations pratiques Dates : du 19 novembre au 31 janvier Public : tout public, petits et grands Tarif : gratuit Visites guidées : des créneaux peuvent être réservés pour les groupes, notamment les scolaires. Pour organiser une visite guidée ou réserver un créneau pour votre groupe, contactez-nous à l’adresse suivante : com.lps@universite-paris-saclay.fr . Alors, prêts à explorer l’invisible et à manipuler la matière ? Une exposition conçue et réalisée au Laboratoire de Physique des Solides (CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay) Conception et coordination : Veronika Kysil Création graphique et décors peints à la main : Diana Tkachenko Chargée de communication avec les scolaires : Khayam Amir-Bakhtiar Conception et fabrication des dispositifs scientifiques : équipe d’ingénieurs du laboratoire – Yannic Simon, Ismaël Nimaga, Jérémie Sanchez and Sambath Saranga. Avec la contribution des scientifiques et des personnels du laboratoire.

Grâce à la filière FIE et à la proximité immédiate des entreprises, il favorise des échanges directs et enrichissants avec les acteurs du secteur. Enfin, le Forum de la Photonique constituera une occasion privilégiée pour les entreprises de découvrir ce lieu entièrement dédié à l’innovation et aux synergies entre formation, recherche et industrie. title: La vie de recherche : Jean Jouzel
description: Signe des temps et de l’importance croissante de cette discipline, cette première rencontre accueille le climatologue Jean Jouzel. Directeur de recherche émérite au CEA, il a consacré l’essentiel de sa carrière à la reconstitution des climats passés. Ses travaux, récompensés par la médaille d’or du CNRS, en font une figure majeure de la climatologie. Membre associé de l’Académie des sciences des États-Unis, il fut vice-président du groupe scientifique du GIEC de 2002 à 2015 et s’est impliqué dans la préparation de la conférence Paris Climat 2015.
location: La Scène de recherche - Théâtre Paris-Saclay

title: Session d’information sur les COST Actions : Comment ces “super GDR européens” peuvent ouvrir vers de nouvelles opportunités de collaborations et projets
description: La participation aux COST Actions, que nous pouvons voir comme des “super GDR européens”, est une voie intéressante pour créer de nouveaux contacts, voire monter de nouvelles collaborations, deux actions nécessaires pour répondre ultérieurement à d’autres appels à projets (AAP) européens (ERC, EIC…). Cela est particulièrement vrai dans un contexte où les AAP européens nécessitent souvent de monter des consortiums multi-partenaires qui incluent des “Widening Countries”. La participation aux COST Actions peut se faire soit dès le montage d’une action en jouant le rôle de de « main proposer » ou de « secondary proposer », soit en rejoignant une Action déjà en cours. Noëlle Gogneau, chercheuse au C2N dans le domaine de la science des matériaux, spécialisée en épitaxie des nanofils III-Nitrures pour les applications en nano-énergie, a coordonné le COST Action OPERA « European Network for Innovative and Advanced Epitaxy » de 2021 à 2025 ( https://cost-opera.eu/ ). Cette action a regroupé 35 pays, a organisé de nombreux workshops et training school, et à financé près de 100 missions scientifiques pour les étudiants et jeunes chercheurs du réseau. A travers de ces actions majeures, de nombreuses nouvelles collaborations ont émergées jouant le rôle de catalyseur pour répondre aux appels à projets. Elle nous parlera des COST Actions de manière générale, des bénéfices de les intégrer — et comment le faire, en s’appuyant sur son expérience de montage et de gestion de l’Action OPERA.

title: Spectacle : Fake news - Un Ennemi du peuple
description: La Scène de recherche présente une pièce grand format pour treize interprètes. Revisitant "Un Ennemi du peuple" d’Henrik Ibsen, "Fake news" s’empare d’une question brûlante : à qui faire confiance ? Dans une ville où l’eau pourrait être contaminée, la parole scientifique se heurte aux intérêts politiques et économiques. Médecin, maire, préfète, journalistes, citoyennes et citoyens : chacun et chacune défend sa version, et le débat s’emballe. Entre assemblée publique et plateau télé, les récits s’affrontent et se déforment. À l’heure des réseaux sociaux, difficile de démêler le vrai du faux. Et si la vérité dépendait de qui parle le plus fort ?

title: Séminaire Charles Vernier
description: Probing the physical properties of matter with light : how confinement at the nanoscale affects the elastic and optical features of materials Materials made of noble metals at the nanoscale are famous for their localized surface plasmon (LSPR) that give colloidal solutions of Au or Ag nanoparticles (NPs) bright, tunable colors. Lesser known are the standing acoustic waves that NPs can sustain in the GHz range. Still, several confined acoustic phonons modes are Raman active and can be detected by using a Brillouin spectrometer [1], needed to access very low frequency range (typically Another notable feature of noble metals NPs is the ability to confine light in a sub-wavelength space. This can be done by fine tuning of LSPR bands, which vary strongly depending on the shape and size of the NPs. It is also possible to increase light-matter coupling by building nanocavities that confine light in few nm cavities [4], typically by using NPs oligomers or NP on a mirror configuration, as shown on the right side of the figure. Such cavities yield sharp, tunable resonances, whose asymmetry can be controlled. How? More on that at my seminar, on Friday, December 4th. (1) Duval, E. Sensitivity of Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance and Acoustic Vibrations to Edge Rounding in Silver Nanocubes. ACS Nano 2023. (3) Portales, H.; Goubet, N.; Saviot, L.; Adichtchev, S.; Murray, D. B.; Mermet, A.; Duval, E.; Pileni, M.-P. Probing Atomic Ordering and Multiple Twinning in Metal Nanocrystals through Their Vibrations. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2008, 105 (39), 14784–14789. (4) Baumberg, J. J.; Aizpurua, J.; Mikkelsen, M. H.; Smith, D. R. Extreme Nanophotonics from Ultrathin Metallic Gaps. Nat. title: Quantum Networks Summit 2027
description: Towards Fully Quantum Networks The Fourth Edition of the Quantum Networks Summit will take place on April 7 & 8, 2027 , at the Palais des Congrès de Paris. Co-located with the Upperside World Congress, the Summit brings together leading experts from industry, research organizations, telecom operators, technology vendors and public institutions to discuss the evolution of quantum networking and quantum-safe infrastructures. Over the past three editions, the event has established itself as one of the leading international forums dedicated to quantum communications, quantum security and the future of network infrastructures. The early registration is open! 2027 Agenda: Quantum Memories, Repeaters, Transducers, Entanglement Distribution There has been more movement in the last twelve months than in the prior three years combined. In this respect, the technology axis will be the primary structure of the 2027 programme. Participants will discuss the relevance of Quantum technologies for classical networking and classical computing with specific highlights on quantum memories, repeaters, transducers and entanglement distribution. Three layers of presentations will be proposed, in the natural progression telcos face when responding to quantum: Layer 1 : Changing the protocols. Layer 2 : The "use quantum primitives inside a classical network" layer. Layer 3 : The network itself becomes quantum. The Call for Papers is open until September 18th. title: OPTDIAG 2027 - rendez-vous du 19 au 21 mai 2027 à Paris !
description: OPTDIAG 2027 - rendez-vous du 19 au 21 mai 2027 à Paris ! OPTDIAG 2027, les Journées du Club PSV – Photonique et Sciences du Vivant, se tiendront du 19 au 21 mai 2027 à l’Institut Langevin , à Paris, à l’initiative de la Société Française d’Optique. Pendant trois jours, chercheurs, ingénieurs, doctorants, étudiants et industriels se retrouveront autour des dernières avancées en imagerie, microscopie, spectroscopie, interaction lumière–matière biologique, ainsi que des applications médicales et agronomiques. Au programme : présentations scientifiques, conférences, communications orales et posters, rencontres entre les mondes académique et industriel et expositions. Le tout dans une atmosphère conviviale, propice aux échanges et aux collaborations. Le programme sera très prochainement disponible. Suivez-nous pour ne rien manquer !

title: Advances in Quantum Cryptography, Paris
description: This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on mathematical developments in Advances in Quantum Cryptography (QCRYPTO). September 13th to December 10th, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris ** REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE ** Deadline for financial support request is March 15, 2027 Presentation of the programme Quantum cryptography lies at the intersection of cryptography, quantum information, and computational complexity. Quantum technologies offer new cryptographic possibilities, while also changing our understanding of which security guarantees and computational tasks are achievable. Recent developments have revealed deep connections between these areas, but many fundamental questions remain open. This programme will bring together researchers from theoretical computer science, mathematics, cryptography, and quantum information. It will explore three closely connected directions: information-theoretic foundations, including quantum communication, nonlocality, randomness, and device-independent security; complexity-theoretic foundations, including quantum proofs, verification, reductions, and computational assumptions; and computational and interactive primitives, including commitments, zero knowledge, secure computation, and protocols involving quantum devices. Through an introductory school, seminars, focused workshops, informal discussions, and extended research visits, the programme aims to develop a common language across neighboring communities. It will provide opportunities for sustained collaboration between senior and junior researchers, encourage new research partnerships, and help identify important directions for the next stage of quantum cryptography. Preliminary list of participants TBD Timeline for the trimester: September 13 to 17 - Introductory school at IHP, Paris, amphitheater Hermite October 11 to 15 - Workshop 1 at IHP, Paris: Advances in Quantum Cryptography: Information-theoretic Foundations November 15 to 19 - Workshop 2 at IHP, Paris: Advances in Quantum Cryptography: Complexity-theoretic Foundations November 29 to December 3 - Workshop 3 at IHP, Paris: Advances in Quantum Cryptography: Computational and Interactive Primitives Organising committee: Prabhanjan Ananth (UCSB)Anne Broadbent (University of Ottawa)Céline Chevalier (Université Paris-Panthéon-Assas, ENS)Alex B. Grilo (CNRS, Sorbonne Université) Scientific committee: Kai-Min Chung (Academia Sinica)Claude Crépeau (McGill University)Eleni Diamanti (CNRS, Sorbonne Université)Yael Tauman Kalai (Microsoft Research, MIT)Elham Kashefi (CNRS, Sorbonne Université)Cecilia Lancien (CNRS, Université Grenoble Alpes)Christian Majenz (DTU)Maria Naya-Plasencia (Inria)Christian Schaffner (University of Amsterdam, QuSoft)Marco Tomamichel (CQT, NUS)Vinod Vaikuntanathan (MIT)Henry Yuen (Columbia University) Back to the thematic trimester main page ------------------------------------ Programme coordinated by the Centre Emile Borel at IHP Sorbonne Université, CNRS IMPORTANT WARNING: Scam / Phishing / SMiShing ! Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. IHP and the organizers will NEVER contact you by phone on this issue and will NEVER ask you to pay for accommodation/ board / possible registration fee in advance.

title: QUEST-IS 2027 — Quantum Engineering Conference and Exhibition
description: In the heart of French deep-tech, academia, and industry, following the success of the 2025 edition, QUEST-IS 2027, the 2nd International Quantum Engineering Conference and Exhibition , will bring together numerous companies from across the global quantum ecosystem. The event will address key technical topics including quantum computing and algorithms, quantum sensing, quantum communications, cryptography and the quantum internet, as well as enabling technologies, with a strong focus on Quantum Engineering for citizen-oriented applications. This multidisciplinary event will provide a unique opportunity for attendees from diverse backgrounds to discuss the technical challenges of applied quantum technologies and explore emerging business opportunities.
